memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Esau looked up and saw the women and children. 'Who are these with you?' he asked. Jacob answered, 'They are the children God has graciously given your servant.' Then the female servants and their children approached and bowed down. Next, Leah and her children came and bowed down. Last of all came Joseph and Rachel, and they too bowed down." - Gen 33:5-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When Esau sees the women and children and asks who they are, listen to how Jacob answers: "They are the children God has graciously given your servant." Notice that little word — graciously. Jacob does not boast, "These are the results of my hard work," or "This is what I earned in twenty years." He sees his family as a gift of God's grace.

This is a mark of how much Jacob has changed. The man who once grabbed and schemed for everything now speaks the language of grace. He recognises that the good in his life came not from his own cleverness but from God's kindness. Later in this same chapter he will say it again: "God has been gracious to me and I have all I need" (v.11).

What a healthy way to view our blessings. Our families, our homes, our work, our very lives — these are gifts of God's grace, not trophies of our own achievement. When we see them this way, gratitude replaces pride, and contentment replaces striving.

Take a moment to look at the good things in your life. Can you name them, as Jacob did, as things "God has graciously given"? Everything we have is a gift from His hand (Jas 1:17). Learning to say "graciously given" turns our whole life into an occasion for thanksgiving.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I see my blessings as things "God has graciously given"?
2. Where has pride in my achievements crowded out gratitude?
3. What good gifts can I thank God for today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that everything good in my life is Your gracious gift. Replace my pride with gratitude, and help me to see my blessings as grace from Your hand. Amen.
